sorting/01_insertion_sort.algorithm:
a = copy of nums
for i from 1 to len(a) - 1:
    key = a[i]
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and a[j] > key:   (j may reach 0: the first element can shift too)
        a[j + 1] = a[j]
        j = j - 1
    a[j + 1] = key
return a

sorting/02_merge_sort.algorithm:
merge(left, right):
    out = [], i = 0, j = 0
    while both runs have elements left:
        if left[i] <= right[j]: append left[i], i = i + 1   (<= so the left wins ties: stable)
        else: append right[j], j = j + 1
    append the rest of left, then the rest of right
    return out
merge_sort(nums):
    if len(nums) <= 1: return a copy
    mid = len(nums) // 2
    left = merge_sort(nums[:mid]), right = merge_sort(nums[mid:])
    return merge(left, right)

sorting/03_quick_sort.algorithm:
partition(a, lo, hi):
    pivot = a[hi], i = lo - 1
    for j from lo to hi - 1:   (stop before hi: the pivot itself must not be swapped)
        if a[j] <= pivot: i = i + 1, swap a[i] and a[j]
    swap a[i + 1] and a[hi]
    return i + 1
sort_range(a, lo, hi):
    if lo < hi:
        p = partition(a, lo, hi)
        sort_range(a, lo, p - 1), sort_range(a, p + 1, hi)
quick_sort(nums):
    a = copy of nums, sort_range(a, 0, len(a) - 1), return a

sorting/04_heap_sort.algorithm:
sift_down(a, i, size):
    loop:
        child = 2 * i + 1
        if child + 1 < size and a[child + 1] > a[child]: child = child + 1
        if child >= size or a[child] <= a[i]: return
        swap a[i] and a[child], i = child
heap_sort(nums):
    a = copy of nums, n = len(a)
    for i from n // 2 - 1 down to 0: sift_down(a, i, n)
    for end from n - 1 down to 1:
        swap a[0] and a[end]
        sift_down(a, 0, end)   (sift inside the shrunk heap a[:end], not the whole array)
    return a

sorting/05_counting_and_bucket_sort.algorithm:
counting_sort(nums):
    if nums is empty: return []
    counts = [0] * (max(nums) + 1)   (values run 0..max inclusive)
    for x in nums: counts[x] = counts[x] + 1
    out = []
    for value from 0 to len(counts) - 1: append value counts[value] times
    return out
bucket_sort(xs):
    n = len(xs), buckets = n empty lists
    for x in xs: append x to buckets[int(x * n)]
    out = []
    for bucket in buckets: append sorted(bucket)   (a bucket groups nearby values; still sort it)
    return out

sorting/06_python_sort_keys_and_stabilit.algorithm:
dept_then_salary_desc(record): return (dept, -salary)   (negating flips just that field)
salary_of(record): return salary
dept_of(record): return dept
sort_one_pass(records):
    return sorted(records, key = dept_then_salary_desc)
sort_two_passes(records):
    by_salary = sorted(records, key = salary_of, descending)
    return sorted(by_salary, key = dept_of)   (sort the output of the first pass; stable keeps it)

searches/01_binary_search_variants.algorithm:
binary_search(nums, x):
    lo = 0, hi = len(nums) - 1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] == x: return mid
        if nums[mid] < x: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid - 1
    return -1
lower_bound(nums, x):
    lo = 0, hi = len(nums)   (hi may be the answer: "no such index" is len(nums))
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] < x: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid
    return lo
upper_bound(nums, x): same loop with nums[mid] <= x
count_of(nums, x): return upper_bound(nums, x) - lower_bound(nums, x)

searches/02_binary_search_on_answer.algorithm:
can_ship(weights, days, cap):
    ships = 1, load = 0
    for w in weights:
        if load + w > cap: ships = ships + 1, load = 0
        load = load + w
    return ships <= days
ship_within_days(weights, days):
    lo = max(weights), hi = sum(weights)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if can_ship(weights, days, mid): hi = mid   (mid works; a smaller capacity might too)
        else: lo = mid + 1
    return lo

searches/03_bfs_grid_shortest_path.algorithm:
rows, cols = size of grid
if grid[0][0] == 1: return -1
dist = {(0, 0): 1}, queue = [(0, 0)]
while the queue is not empty:
    (r, c) = pop the front
    if (r, c) is the bottom-right: return dist[(r, c)]
    for each of the four neighbours (nr, nc):
        skip if out of bounds
        skip if grid[nr][nc] == 1 or (nr, nc) already in dist
        dist[(nr, nc)] = dist[(r, c)] + 1   (mark when enqueued, or cells get queued twice)
        push (nr, nc)
return -1

searches/05_connected_components.algorithm:
build_adjacency(n, edges):
    adj = n empty lists
    for (a, b) in edges: append b to adj[a], append a to adj[b]
    return adj
count_components(n, edges):
    adj = build_adjacency(n, edges), seen = {}, count = 0
    for start from 0 to n - 1:
        if start in seen: continue
        count = count + 1   (a fresh start node means a brand-new component)
        add start to seen, queue = [start]
        while the queue is not empty:
            node = pop the front
            for neighbour in adj[node] not in seen: add to seen, push neighbour
    return count

graphs/01_adjacency_list_bfs_dfs.algorithm:
build_adjacency(n, edges, directed):
    adj = n empty lists
    for (u, v) in edges: append v to adj[u]; if not directed also append u to adj[v]
    sort each list, return adj
bfs(adj, source):
    order = [], seen = {source}, queue = [source]
    while the queue is not empty:
        node = pop the front, append node to order
        for neighbour in adj[node] not in seen: add to seen, push neighbour   (mark on enqueue)
    return order
dfs(adj, source):
    order = [], seen = {}, stack = [source]
    while the stack is not empty:
        node = pop the top
        if node in seen: continue
        add node to seen, append node to order
        for neighbour in reversed(adj[node]) not in seen: push neighbour
    return order

graphs/02_topological_sort_kahn_and_dfs.algorithm:
build_adjacency(n, edges): adj = n empty lists; for (u, v) in edges append v to adj[u]
topological_sort_kahn(n, edges):
    adj = build_adjacency(n, edges), indegree[v] = number of edges into v
    queue = every node with indegree 0, order = []
    while the queue is not empty:
        node = pop the front, append node to order
        for neighbour in adj[node]:
            indegree[neighbour] = indegree[neighbour] - 1
            if indegree[neighbour] == 0: push neighbour
    if len(order) < n: return []   (nodes never reached indegree 0: a cycle)
    return order
visit(adj, node, color, post):
    color[node] = grey
    for neighbour in adj[node]:
        if grey: return false; if white and not visit(adj, neighbour, color, post): return false
    color[node] = black, append node to post, return true
topological_sort_dfs(n, edges):
    adj = build_adjacency(n, edges), color = all white, post = []
    for node from 0 to n - 1: if white and not visit(adj, node, color, post): return []
    return post reversed

graphs/03_union_find.algorithm:
make_sets(n): parent = [0, 1, ..., n - 1], size = [1] * n
find(parent, x):
    if parent[x] != x: parent[x] = find(parent, parent[x])   (path compression: point x at the root)
    return parent[x]
union(parent, size, a, b):
    root_a = find(a), root_b = find(b)
    if root_a == root_b: return false
    if size[root_a] < size[root_b]: swap root_a and root_b
    parent[root_b] = root_a, size[root_a] = size[root_a] + size[root_b]
    return true
connected(parent, a, b): return find(a) == find(b)
count_components(parent): count the x with parent[x] == x

graphs/04_kruskal_mst.algorithm:
find(parent, x):
    while parent[x] != x: parent[x] = parent[parent[x]], x = parent[x]
    return x
kruskal(n, edges):
    by_weight = (w, u, v) for every edge, sorted
    parent = [0, 1, ..., n - 1], total = 0, tree = []
    for (w, u, v) in by_weight:
        root_u = find(u), root_v = find(v)
        if root_u == root_v: continue   (already connected: this edge would close a cycle)
        parent[root_u] = root_v
        total = total + w, append (u, v, w) to tree
        if len(tree) == n - 1: break
    return (total, tree)
